Private Capital, UAE & GCC

Good money needs a good reason.

Bolshoi Partners is a private capital advisory. We prepare businesses for capital, build the investment case, identify who should see it, and manage the process from first review through investor dialogue.

The value is in the match between a business and the capital that actually fits it, not in the size of a contact list.

How It Works

Three stages. Each one produces something you keep.

01

Investor Sanity Check

We look at the business the way an investor would: investment logic, the numbers, governance, risk, whether it would hold up under real diligence, and who its natural investors actually are.

What you get: a private diagnostic dashboard showing what to protect, what to fix, and what capital is likely to question first.

02

Investor Mapping

Once the business holds up, the question changes: which capital should back it, in what structure, and why. Different capital has different mandates and different reasons to back the same business. We work out which types fit, what stake and structure make sense for each, and how the deal is packaged financially before anyone sees it.

What you get: a distinct case, and a distinct offer, for each type of capital that fits.

03

Investor Visibility Management

We run the process itself: the narrative adapted for each type of capital, named decision-makers, and a Match Note behind every introduction, explaining why this investor, why this business, why now.

What you get: coordinated investor conversations, each one accountable to a stated reason, and terms aligned to what actually closes.

Both Sides Of The Table

One standard, read two ways.

For businesses, relevance comes before reach: the right capital, not the longest list. For investors, fewer opportunities arrive, each one already read against a stated focus.

Selective By Design

A small number of mandates, on purpose.

Bolshoi works on a deliberately limited number of mandates at any time. Every opportunity is screened personally before it is accepted, and every introduction follows an approved thesis rather than a distribution list.

Do We Fit

Sector agnostic. Geography agnostic. Economics matter more.

Who can use the Sanity Check. Established private businesses and asset owners with real, verifiable economics. No active fundraising process is required.

Who we take into capital mandates. Active capital requirements typically start at approximately USD 3 million. We do not select mandates by sector; we look for a real economic engine, a credible use of capital, and enough underlying substance for an investor to make a serious decision.

What Matters To Us

Scalable economics. Capital has a credible route to creating materially greater enterprise value, whatever form that takes for this business.

Understandable model. We can identify who pays, why they pay, where the margin comes from and how the economics work.

Verifiable fundamentals. Revenue, assets, ownership and material operating claims can ultimately be evidenced.

Clean legal footing. The company, assets, ownership and contemplated transaction can withstand normal compliance and diligence.

Aligned principals. The owners and authorised decision-makers are accessible and prepared to run a disciplined process.

Clear use of funds. There is a specific reason for raising capital and a credible account of what it changes.

Your materials do not need to be perfect. Your underlying business does need to be real.

Scalability, in this sense, is broad by design. A software business scales through customer growth. A mining asset scales through de-risking, development and production. An industrial company scales through new capacity, a real asset through development or repositioning, a platform through consolidation. The physics differ. The common denominator does not: capital needs an identifiable mechanism for creating value.

What Changes

Once Bolshoi is involved.

The story is rebuilt around what each audience actually needs to hear, not one deck sent everywhere. The investors that see it are the ones with a real reason to look, not the longest list of contacts. Every conversation that follows carries that reason with it, so it starts from relevance rather than a cold read.

What You Receive

Three products. One sequence.

Investor Sanity Check. A private diagnostic dashboard and investor readback, including anonymised real-investor feedback where appropriate, expressly approved and feasible.

Investor Mapping. A capital map, a deal architecture and a diligence blueprint, defining who to approach, on what terms, and what they will need to see.

Investor Visibility Management. Managed outreach, Match Notes and a running Visibility Ledger, with feedback folded back in as it comes.

How Engagement Works

Review first. Mandate after.

Most relationships begin with the Sanity Check below. Where an Investor Visibility Management mandate follows, it is structured around a four-month initial commitment, with scope agreed after the review. A poor deck, an incomplete data room or the wrong capital already in the mix are all fixable. We can fix readiness. We cannot manufacture a business underneath it.

Investor Sanity Check

See your business through capital's eyes.

A complimentary, confidential review of how your business is likely to read to investors today, useful whether or not you are raising.

Request a Sanity Check →

What an investor would actually think if your business landed on their desk tomorrow. It reads on the same things a lender, a partner or a buyer eventually will.

Eight Lenses, One Question

The framework, not a result. Hover or tap a lens.

01

Investment Logic

Whether the commercial argument holds together on a first read, without a call to explain it.

02

Revenue & Cash Quality

Whether revenue is recurring, concentrated or lumpy, and how closely it converts to cash.

03

Margin & Unit Economics

Whether the economics of the business hold up at the unit level, not just in aggregate.

04

Scalability & Capital Efficiency

Whether growth requires proportionate capital, or compounds more efficiently than that.

05

Balance Sheet & Funding Logic

Whether the existing capital structure makes sense, and what new capital would actually fix.

06

Governance & Ownership

Whether the cap table and decision rights are clean enough to move quickly.

07

Evidence & Diligence Readiness

Whether the claims can be checked, or rest on the deck alone.

08

Investor & Strategic Fit

Who this naturally fits, and how far current positioning sits from them.

Shows what is assessed, not a score. Nothing here is computed until a real business is reviewed.

Investor Mapping

Different capital. Different reasons to back the same business.

Once a business holds up, the next question is which capital should back it, in what structure, and why.

The facts do not change. The investment case does.

A family office, a strategic corporate, a private equity fund and a credit investor can look at the identical business and see four different opportunities. This is where we work out which of them actually fit, what each would need to hear, and what to offer them.

Why This Comes Second

After the Sanity Check, before any introduction.

The Sanity Check confirms the business is sound and not afraid of scrutiny. This is what happens next: deciding who it actually belongs in front of, and building the case for each of them, before Investor Visibility Management puts any of it into motion.

Investor Editions

The same business. Six different reasons to back it.

Choose a type to see the reason that actually moves them, and how they tend to behave once they are interested.

Decision Path
Primary Lens
Typical Structure
Information Threshold

Qualitative, not scored. Decision mechanics differ by capital type and institution. A principal-led family office, an investment committee, a strategic corporate and a credit underwriter may require different evidence, sequencing and internal approvals even when reviewing the same company.

What Gets Decided

Not just who. What, and on what terms, in order.

01

Identify which capital fits

Not just the category. The actual family offices, funds and individuals worth approaching for this specific business.

Deliverable: a named list of who is actually worth approaching.

02

Decide the stake and structure

Minority or majority, equity or credit, outright sale or partnership, matched to who is being approached.

Deliverable: a recommended structure and stake for each name on the list.

03

Package the deal

The financial framing, the valuation logic, the use-of-proceeds story, built for each edition before it is shown to anyone.

Deliverable: investor-ready materials, tailored per edition, handed to Investor Visibility Management.

Mapping decides who, and builds the case for each. Approaching them is what Investor Visibility Management does next.

Completion Economics

Typically 2–5% of capital successfully closed, stepping down as transaction size increases, agreed within the applicable regulated structure before outreach begins. Debt and structured credit mandates are typically priced lower. Final economics depend on structure, complexity and mandate scope.

About

Every introduction needs a thesis.

Most businesses manage how customers see them. Almost none manage how capital sees them.

Bolshoi Partners exists to give that version of a business the same discipline. We are based in the UAE and work across GCC and MENA private capital, on a small number of mandates at a time by design, not by accident.

How Mandates Are Run

A principal-led practice.

Bolshoi is run as a small, deliberately limited practice rather than a platform. Every mandate is reviewed personally before it is accepted, and every investor conversation is coordinated by someone who has read the specific situation directly, not generated by a system.

Who Runs It

Taisiya Presnyakova

Founder, Bolshoi Partners
Dubai, UAE

Every mandate Bolshoi accepts is reviewed personally before it begins, and every capital map, deal architecture and investor conversation runs through the same principal-led standard described on this site.

How We Think

Asked privately, before anything is shown to anyone.

—Who should actually see this business.
—Why them, and not a longer list.
—What they will notice first, and what will concern them.
—What would give them a genuine reason to back it.
—How the first conversation should be framed.

An introduction made without answering these is distribution with better formatting.

Direct Mandate Standard

We work with principals, not chains of intermediaries.

Before accepting a mandate, we confirm who owns the business, who is authorised to give the mandate, who else is already involved, and where a conflict might sit. In practice, that means we do not take on situations with unclear ownership, conflicting shareholders, long chains of intermediaries, or financials that cannot be verified. We can decline a mandate, and sometimes do.

Good money needs a good reason. We make sure yours is understood.

Privacy & Regulatory Disclosure

How your information is handled.

What we collect, why, and who it is shared with.

Bolshoi Partners is based in the UAE and processes personal data in accordance with the UAE's federal data protection framework. This page explains what is collected through this site, why, and how it is handled. It is a plain-English summary, not a substitute for the full policy your counterparty agreement or engagement letter will reference.

What We Collect

Only what a form asks for.

Contact details. Name, email, organisation, and website where provided.

Situation details. What you tell us about the business, the capital sought, structure preferences, or investment criteria, depending on which form you use.

Technical data. Standard information any website receives when a page is requested, such as browser type and referring page.

We do not ask for, and you should not send, highly confidential material through a contact form. Where supporting documents are needed, a secure exchange is arranged directly.

Why We Collect It

To review your enquiry, and nothing beyond that.

Purpose. Information submitted through this site is used to review and respond to your enquiry, and, where a mandate proceeds, to carry it out.

Retention. Enquiry details are retained only as long as relevant to the purpose they were collected for, or as required by law.

Sharing. Information is not sold or distributed to third parties for marketing. Where a mandate involves a regulated financial service, relevant details are shared with the appropriately licensed partner carrying out that specific activity, under confidentiality obligations.

International transfers. Where information is processed outside the UAE, for example by a service provider, appropriate safeguards are applied.

Your Rights

Ask, correct, or ask us to stop.

You can ask what information we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it, subject to any legal or contractual obligation to retain it. To make a request, or for any question about how your information is handled, contact us directly →.
